sentence: This project uses optical imaging to study how loss of synaptic function is linked to the amyloid peptide and genotype in aging and Alzheimer's disease.
This project builds a tool that combines weather, environmental and mosquito data to predict where and when malaria outbreaks are likely to occur.
This project uses liquid biopsy samples of plasma to track tumor DNA and RNA changes as patients with colorectal and anal cancers respond to treatment.
This project builds tools that predict how function, cognition and quality of life change for older adults with advanced lung cancer during chemotherapy or immunotherapy.
This project studies how circular pieces of DNA outside chromosomes form, work and help cancers resist treatment.
This project studies how cells and circuits produce persistent neural activity, which is thought to be the basis of working memory.
This project finds hotspots of HIV among people who inject drugs and tests an intervention that improves access to prevention and drug treatment materials.
This project uses mouse models and imaging to find out what a protein required for spermatid elongation does in sperm development.
This project studies the structure and function of channels that sense mechanical force and channels that carry magnesium.
This project studies regulators that control the balance between proliferation and differentiation in the skin epidermis.
This project builds a small fluorescence microscope that can image calcium activity through an intact skull in mice.
This project studies how proton pumps called vacuolar ATPases are assembled, made, regulated and put to work in cells.
This project tests whether a treatment helps T cells recognize and kill cells infected with HIV, and why some viral subtypes resist it.
This project tries to find out what marks accelerated cardiac aging in survivors of adolescent and young adult cancer.
This project provides shared support for vision research, including image analysis, biostatistics and genetic analysis.
This project studies how bacteriophages interact with bacteria, including defense systems that shape phage host range.
This project provides genomics, kinomics and data analysis support to researchers studying tumors linked to neurofibromatosis type 1.
This project builds contractile conduits from stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes, fibroblasts and endothelial cells to treat single ventricle heart defects, and tests them in rats.
This project uses zebrafish and mouse cancer models to understand how infantile rhabdomyosarcoma develops and to find targets for treatment.
This project describes the traits and tumor biology linked to inherited variants in succinate dehydrogenase genes to estimate risk and evaluate targeted therapies.
